tricks.hook: Census for the denominator, SRS for the rate, CRS for the certificate

scenes.title: Before the lesson — four things it will assume
scenes.objective: Have the rates, the fertility measures and the life table ready, so the institutional facts attach to quantities you can compute.
body: This topic has two halves that are examined differently. The institutional half — who runs the census, under which Act, on what date — is recall. The measurement half — birth rates, fertility measures, life tables — is arithmetic, and it is where the marks are easier to secure because they do not depend on remembering a year.
The four checks below are the measurement half. Get them solid and the rest of the lesson is a set of names and dates hung on quantities you can already produce.

items.ask: Define the crude birth rate, crude death rate, infant mortality rate and maternal mortality ratio, and say what denominator each uses.
items.recall: CBR and CDR are events per 1,000 mid-year population. IMR is deaths under one year per 1,000 LIVE BIRTHS. MMR is maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births. The natural growth rate is CBR minus CDR.
refresh: The trap is the denominator, not the formula. CBR and CDR are per 1,000 of the whole population, which is why they are called crude: they take no account of the age structure. IMR and MMR are per live births, because infant and maternal deaths are events of childbearing, not of the population at large.

MMR additionally uses a different multiplier, 1,00,000 rather than 1,000, because maternal deaths are rare. India's MMR of 93 and IMR of 25 are therefore not on the same scale at all, and a question that asks you to compare them is testing exactly that.
Keep the word ratio for MMR. It is a ratio because the denominator — live births — does not contain the population at risk of a maternal death, which is pregnancies, not births.

items.ask: Define GFR, ASFR, TFR, GRR and NRR, and give the relations between them.
items.recall: GFR = births per 1,000 women aged 15-49. ASFR is the same, computed within an age group. TFR = sum of ASFRs across the reproductive span, times the width of each age group — the number of children a woman would bear under current rates. GRR = TFR × proportion of births that are female. NRR = GRR × probability of a girl surviving to the mean age of childbearing.
refresh: The sequence refines a single idea. GFR fixes the crude birth rate's worst fault by using only women of reproductive age. ASFR then splits that by age, so the measure no longer depends on how women are distributed across the span. TFR sums the ASFRs into one number with a meaning you can state in words.

GRR narrows TFR to daughters, because only daughters reproduce in the next generation. NRR narrows it again by letting some of those daughters die before they reproduce, so NRR = 1 is exactly replacement: each generation reproduces itself. NRR < 1 means an eventual decline, however large the current population.
With five-year age groups, TFR = 5 × Σ ASFR, with ASFRs expressed per woman. Forgetting the factor of 5, or forgetting to divide by 1,000, is the most common arithmetic slip in this topic.

items.ask: What is a life table, and what do the columns lₓ, dₓ, qₓ and eₓ mean?
items.recall: A table that follows a hypothetical cohort through mortality at current age-specific rates. lₓ is the number surviving to exact age x; dₓ the deaths between x and x+1; qₓ the probability of dying in that interval; and eₓ the expectation of life at age x. An abridged life table uses five-year intervals instead of single years.
refresh: The life table turns a set of age-specific death rates into a single intelligible statement: given today's mortality, how long would a newborn live. That is e₀, life expectancy at birth, and it is a property of the current rates, not a forecast about anyone alive.
The internal relations are worth carrying: dₓ = lₓ − lₓ₊₁, and qₓ = dₓ / lₓ. Everything else in the table is built from the lₓ column and the person-years lived, Lₓ.
The SRS publishes abridged life tables for India using five-year aggregates of its own data, which is why the life table belongs in this topic and not only in a methods paper.

items.ask: What is the difference between de jure and de facto enumeration, and between a crude and a standardised rate?
items.recall: De facto counts a person where they actually are at the reference moment; de jure counts them at their usual place of residence. A crude rate divides events by the whole population; a standardised rate reweights age-specific rates to a common age distribution so that two populations can be compared.
refresh: India's census is essentially de facto, built on a single reference moment, which is why the reference moment matters so much and why houseless people are enumerated on a separate, specified night.

Standardisation exists because a crude death rate is as much a statement about age structure as about mortality. A retirement town and a university town can have identical age-specific death rates and very different crude rates. Direct standardisation applies the two populations' age-specific rates to one standard age distribution; indirect standardisation applies a standard set of rates to the two age distributions.
This is the reason the exam asks for crude rates and for TFR in the same breath. One is contaminated by structure and the other is not.

scenes.title: Three systems counting the same events
scenes.objective: See why India runs a census, a registration system and a sample survey at once, and what each is for.
body: Births and deaths are counted three times over in India, by three different systems, and the exam's questions almost always turn on which of the three a figure came from.

The census is a stock. Once a decade it counts every person where they are at a single reference moment, and that is the only operation that produces a true denominator — the population itself, by age, sex, district and village. It is enormously expensive and therefore rare.

The Civil Registration System is a flow, and in principle a complete one. Every birth and death is supposed to be registered with a local registrar within 21 days, by law. Complete registration would make a sample survey unnecessary, and India's registration is now reported at 99.1% birth registration and 99.4% death registration in 2024 — but those figures are themselves computed against survey-based estimates, the coverage varies sharply by state, and the data arrive with about a two-year lag.

The Sample Registration System is the third: a flow measured on a sample, by a method designed to catch the events that registration misses. It exists because India needed reliable birth and death rates long before registration was anywhere near complete, and it is still the source of every rate you are asked to quote — CBR, CDR, IMR, TFR, MMR.

So the division of labour is: the census gives the denominator, the SRS gives the rates, the CRS gives the legal record of each individual event. A question asking where a figure came from is asking which of those three jobs it belongs to.

aside.h: The sentence to carry into the exam
aside.body: Census = stock, decennial, complete. CRS = flow, continuous, legal, complete in principle. SRS = flow, continuous, on a sample, and the actual source of India's vital rates.

ask.q: If civil registration reached 100% completeness tomorrow, would the Sample Registration System become redundant?
ask.nudge: Ask what the SRS measures that a register of events cannot, and how you would know that registration had in fact reached 100%.

scenes.title: The census — history, law and the 2027 round
scenes.objective: Give the census's history, its legal and constitutional basis, its organisation, and the 2027 schedule.

blocks.body: The first census of India was taken in 1872, but not synchronously: different parts of the country were enumerated at different times. The first synchronous census — the whole country at one reference moment — was 1881, and censuses have been decennial since. The organisation was set up afresh for each census, on an ad-hoc basis, until 1951.

The Census Act, 1948 provides the legal framework and defines the duties and powers of census officers; section 15 makes the information given by an individual confidential and inadmissible as evidence. The Census Rules, 1990 sit under it. In May 1949 the Government decided to create a permanent organisation under the Registrar General of India, who is ex-officio Census Commissioner, in the Ministry of Home Affairs. Census is a Union subject, entry 69 of the Union List in the Seventh Schedule.

blocks.h: Census 2027 — the schedule as notified by 12 November 2026
blocks.body: The census due in 2021 was postponed during the pandemic. Census 2027 is India's 16th census and the 8th since Independence. Phase I Houselisting and Housing Census was notified for 1 April to 30 September 2026. Population Enumeration (Phase II) is governed by later area-specific Gazette notifications: do not memorise February 2027 as one uniform window for every State and Union Territory.

blocks.h: The later schedule for four election-bound States / areas
blocks.body: ORGI's 5 September 2026 notification schedules Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand for self-enumeration 16–30 November 2026, Population Enumeration 1 December 2026–4 January 2027 and revisional round 5–9 January 2027. Other regions follow their own ORGI Gazette notifications.

blocks.h: Reference moments are not fieldwork windows
blocks.body: The national reference moment is 00:00 hours on 1 March 2027. ORGI has separate provisions for Ladakh and snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, with a 1 October 2026 reference moment. These reference moments define the date to which population particulars refer; they are not interchangeable with the dates on which enumerators visit households.

It is India's first digital census. Houselisting uses a mobile application that works offline and uploads later; an optional self-enumeration portal is available in sixteen languages and issues an SE ID that the enumerator uses to confirm the household's entry. Caste is enumerated, following the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs decision of 30 April 2025, during Phase II. The operation engages about 31 lakh enumerators and supervisors, over one lakh census functionaries and around 18,600 technical staff.

First, 1872 is the first census and 1881 the first SYNCHRONOUS one; a question naming one wants the other as the distractor. Second, the permanent census organisation dates from 1949, not from the Act of 1948 and not from 1951, though the office functioned from 1951. Third, the census sits with the Ministry of Home Affairs under the RGI, not with MoSPI — the whole of the rest of Unit X is MoSPI, and this topic is the exception.

scenario.teaser: A census due in 2021 held in 2027 — and everything downstream that had to run on 2011 numbers meanwhile.
scenario.title: Sixteen years between counts
body: India's censuses have been decennial since 1881, through two world wars, partition and every emergency since. The 2021 round was the first to be missed. Houselisting had been scheduled for April 2020; the pandemic intervened, and the operation was postponed repeatedly until the schedule for 2027 was announced.

The gap is not merely a missing data point, because a census is the only operation that produces a complete population denominator. Every rate in this lesson is events divided by population, and for the whole of that period the population came from projections rolled forward from 2011. Sampling frames for household surveys are built from census villages and urban blocks, so the NSS and the PLFS were drawing from a frame that aged by sixteen years. Delimitation of constituencies, the allocation of seats, and a long list of schemes with population-based entitlements all wait on census figures.

That is the honest case for why the census is the foundation of the rest of Unit X rather than one more survey in it. The consumption survey can be run again; the price index can be rebased; but the denominator underneath all of them is produced once a decade and nothing substitutes for it.

For the exam, carry the stable facts — Census 2027, 16th overall and 8th since Independence — but use the Gazette notification for the relevant State/UT when a question asks for Phase-II fieldwork dates.
scenario.close: A census is the denominator the whole statistical system divides by, which is why a missed one propagates into every rate.

scenes.title: The Civil Registration System and the law behind it
scenes.objective: State the legal basis of registration, distinguish the 2023 and 2026 amendments, and interpret the latest official completeness figures.

blocks.body: The continuous, permanent and compulsory recording of births and deaths as individual legal events. The Office of the Registrar General, India, set up in 1951, oversees it and coordinates with a Chief Registrar of Births and Deaths in each state and union territory; the first annual report using civil registration data appeared in 1958. Registration is done by local registrars, and the informant must report the event within 21 days, at the place where it occurred, with penalties rising for delay.

blocks.h: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
blocks.body: The parent Act, which made registration of births and deaths compulsory throughout India. Before it, registration existed in parts of the country under provincial law and was weakly enforced. The Act is the answer whenever a question asks for the legal basis of birth and death registration in India.

blocks.h: The 2023 amendment — national database and certificate
blocks.body: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 came into force on 1 October 2023. It provides for a national database maintained by the Registrar General and state databases under Chief Registrars; makes the birth certificate a single document admissible as proof of date and place of birth for specified purposes including school admission, driving licences, electoral rolls, Aadhaar, marriage registration and government employment; and provides for use of the database to update the National Population Register, electoral rolls and ration-card records, subject to data-sharing controls.

ORGI's current Vital Statistics Division page describes the parent Act as amended in both 2023 and 2026. The 2026 amendment changes the authority for very late registrations: where information is furnished more than two years after the event, registration requires an order of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class. This is a change to delayed-registration authority, not a change to the ordinary 21-day reporting period.

ORGI reports that the national Vital Statistics based on Civil Registration System report for 2024 was released in July 2026. Registration levels are 99.1% for births and 99.4% for deaths in 2024, compared with 82.4% and 66.4% respectively in 2011. These are completeness levels of event registration; they are not the SRS birth rate, death rate or infant mortality rate.

blocks.h: Two bodies, two jobs, one office
blocks.body: The census and the CRS and the SRS all sit under the Registrar General of India in the Ministry of Home Affairs. What differs is the instrument: the Census Act, 1948 for the census, the RBD Act, 1969 for registration, and no statute at all for the SRS, which is an administrative survey.

items.q: Which year saw India's first census, and which the first synchronous one?
items.a: 1872 for the first census, not held synchronously; 1881 for the first synchronous census. Decennial since.

items.q: Give the Act governing the census and the Act governing registration of births and deaths.
items.a: The Census Act, 1948 for the census; the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 for registration.

items.q: Who conducts the census, and under which ministry?
items.a: The Registrar General of India, ex-officio Census Commissioner, in the Ministry of Home Affairs. The permanent organisation was decided on in May 1949.

items.q: Give the two reference moments for Census 2027.
items.a: 00:00 hours on 1 March 2027 for the country; 00:00 hours on 1 October 2026 for Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

items.q: What did the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 create, and from when?
items.a: A national database of births and deaths under the Registrar General, in force from 1 October 2023, with the birth certificate as a single document of proof.

items.q: Within how many days must a birth or death be reported to the registrar?
items.a: 21 days, at the place where the event occurred.

scenes.title: The Sample Registration System and its dual record method
scenes.objective: Explain how the SRS gets a more complete count than a register, and what it publishes.

blocks.h: Why it exists, and when it started
blocks.body: The SRS was introduced in the 1960s as an interim measure while civil registration was far from complete, and it has outlasted that description. A pilot ran in selected states in 1964-65 and full-scale operations began in 1969-70. It is run by the Office of the Registrar General of India — the same body that takes the census — and it rests on no statute, being an administrative survey rather than a legal register.

blocks.h: The dual record system, which is the examinable core
blocks.body: Two independent records of the same events are made and then compared. First, continuous enumeration: a part-time enumerator resident in the sample unit — typically an anganwadi worker or a teacher — records every birth and death as it occurs, from families, community informants, hospitals and burial or cremation grounds, visiting urban households monthly and rural households quarterly. Second, a half-yearly retrospective survey by a full-time supervisor, independently, with a verbal autopsy form completed for each death.

The Directorate of Census Operations matches the supervisor's list against the enumerator's. Events on one list and not the other, and apparent duplicates, are then verified in the field — by a third person, or by the supervisor and enumerator together. The supervisor also updates the sample unit's population by age, sex and marital status, which supplies the denominators. The reconciled records go to the RGI for national tabulation.

A single register misses events in a pattern, not at random: deaths of the very old and the very young, events in households with no reason to approach a registrar, rural events, events to women. Two independent passes, matched, catch most of what either alone would miss, and the size of the mismatch is itself a measure of how incomplete a single pass would have been. That is the whole logic of the method, and it is the standard answer to 'why not simply use the register'.

By 2023 the SRS covered 8,839 sampling units and over 8.8 million people. The sample is designed so that the infant mortality rate can be estimated with a relative standard error below 15% — a design criterion worth quoting, because it shows the sample size was chosen for a stated precision on a specific indicator rather than picked for convenience.

An annual bulletin with CBR, CDR and IMR; a Statistical Report with fertility and mortality indicators including GFR, ASFR and TFR; special bulletins on maternal mortality and on causes of death, less frequently; and abridged life tables built on five-year aggregates. The UN Population Division and the RGI both use SRS estimates for population projections.

The SRS gives RATES from a sample; the CRS gives COUNTS of individually registered events. The CRS cannot give you a rate without a denominator from the census or a projection, and its completeness is itself measured against SRS rates. If a question gives you a rate for India, it came from the SRS.

scenes.title: The current figures, and what each one says
scenes.objective: Carry India's vital rates with their periods, and read what each implies.

blocks.body: Crude birth rate 18.4 per 1,000, down from 19.1 in 2022. Crude death rate 6.4 per 1,000. Natural growth rate therefore 12.0 per 1,000, which is CBR minus CDR and nothing more. Infant mortality rate 25 per 1,000 live births. Total fertility rate 1.9.

It is below the replacement level of 2.1, which is the TFR at which a population reproduces itself once mortality before the end of childbearing is allowed for — a little above 2 for that reason, not exactly 2. A below-replacement TFR does not mean the population is falling now: India's population continues to grow because of its young age structure, which is called population momentum. The state spread is wide: Bihar highest at 2.8, Delhi lowest at 1.2.

blocks.h: Sex ratio at birth, and the convention
blocks.body: 917 for 2021-23 — females per 1,000 males, averaged over three years because the annual figure is noisy. Chhattisgarh highest at 974, Uttarakhand lowest at 868. Note the convention: India reports the sex ratio as females per 1,000 males, while much international work reports males per 100 females. A question that gives a figure near 1,050 is using the other convention.

93 per 1,00,000 live births for 2019-21, down from 130 for 2014-16. The SDG target is 70 or below by 2030. MMR is published for three-year periods, not single years, because maternal deaths are too rare for an annual sample estimate to be stable — the same reason the multiplier is a lakh rather than a thousand.

Birth rate falling, death rate low and flat, TFR below replacement, infant and maternal mortality falling but still above the SDG targets, and a sex ratio at birth well below the biological norm of about 950. The last is the one figure in the set that is not simply a development story, and an exam question asking which indicator does not fit the pattern of improvement is usually pointing at it.

blocks.h: Period labels are part of the answer
blocks.body: CBR, CDR, IMR and TFR are annual, currently 2023. Sex ratio at birth is a three-year average, currently 2021-23. MMR is a three-year figure, currently 2019-21. Giving a correct number against the wrong period is a wrong answer, and the three different period lengths are deliberate.

scenario.teaser: One of India's vital statistics has a known biological value. Measure it, and the gap is the finding.
scenario.title: The one number with a benchmark
body: Most vital rates have no natural level to compare against. There is no biologically correct birth rate or death rate; a figure is high or low only relative to another country or another year. The sex ratio at birth is the exception, and that is what makes it the most statistically interesting number in this topic.

Across human populations, about 105 boys are born for every 100 girls — a regularity so stable that demographers treat it as a biological constant, though there is no accepted explanation for why it holds. On India's convention of females per 1,000 males, that is about 952. The excess of boys is then reversed by higher male mortality at every later age, which is why women outnumber men in the older age groups.

The SRS reports India's sex ratio at birth as 917 for 2021-23. The gap between 917 and roughly 952 is not sampling error: the SRS sample covers over 8.8 million people, and the figure is averaged over three years precisely to damp the year-to-year noise. A systematic shortfall of that size, sustained over years, is evidence of something acting on the ratio before birth or at registration.

The state spread makes the point sharper. Chhattisgarh reports 974, above the biological value; Uttarakhand reports 868, far below it. A single biological constant cannot vary by state, so the variation is in the behaviour, not in the biology.

For the exam, three things follow. The convention — females per 1,000 males in India, males per 100 females in much international work, so a figure near 1,050 is the other convention. The period — a three-year average, not a single year. And the reading — this is the one indicator in the set that does not fit a story of steady improvement, which is what a question asking for the odd one out is pointing at.
scenario.close: A statistic with a known expected value is worth more than one without: here the benchmark turns a number into a finding.

scenes.title: Compute TFR, GRR and NRR from age-specific rates
scenes.objective: Do the arithmetic the measurement half of this topic actually asks for.
scenes.problem: For a population, the age-specific fertility rates per 1,000 women are: 15-19: 30, 20-24: 120, 25-29: 130, 30-34: 60, 35-39: 20, 40-44: 8, 45-49: 2. The sex ratio at birth is 917 females per 1,000 males, and the probability that a newborn girl survives to the mean age of childbearing is 0.95. Find the TFR, the GRR and the NRR, and say whether the population is replacing itself.
hints: Sum the ASFRs first, then deal with the width of the age groups and the per-1,000 scale.
GRR narrows TFR to daughters only, so you need the proportion of births that are female — not the ratio as given.
The sex ratio is females per 1,000 males, so the proportion female is 917 divided by the total of females and males, not by 1,000.

solution.say: Sum the age-specific rates. The groups are five years wide, so TFR is five times the sum, with the per-1,000 scale divided out.
Convert the sex ratio into a proportion. With 917 females per 1,000 males, every 1,917 births contain 917 females.
GRR is the TFR counting daughters only.
NRR allows for mortality among those daughters before they reach childbearing.

NRR is below 1, so each generation of women is being replaced by about 0.84 of a generation; under these rates the population would eventually decline, even though a young age structure can keep it growing for decades. Note also that TFR = 1.85 is below the replacement level of 2.1, which says the same thing in the cruder measure.

scenes.answer: TFR = 1.85, GRR = 0.885, NRR = 0.841. The population is below replacement.
scenes.check: Three checks that catch most errors. TFR must be a plausible number of children, so a few units, not hundreds — if you got 370 or 1,850 you forgot the per-1,000 scale or the factor of 5. GRR must be a little under half of TFR. NRR must be below GRR, because survival is a probability below 1.

scenes.title: Six statements — verdict on each before you look
scenes.objective: Meet the confusions this topic is built on: the three systems, the denominators and the periods.
scenes.intro: Each is either the standard fact or one detail moved from a neighbour.

items.claim: The census of India is conducted by the Registrar General of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
items.why: The RGI is ex-officio Census Commissioner, and the permanent organisation was decided on in May 1949. The census is the one part of Unit X that does not sit with MoSPI.

items.claim: The first census of India was held in 1881.
items.why: The first census was 1872, held non-synchronously. 1881 is the first SYNCHRONOUS census, and decennial censuses run from there. Both years are correct answers to different questions.

items.claim: The infant mortality rate is the number of deaths under one year per 1,000 mid-year population.
items.why: Per 1,000 LIVE BIRTHS. The crude birth and death rates use mid-year population; IMR does not, and MMR uses live births with a multiplier of a lakh.

items.claim: The Sample Registration System uses a dual record system and is run by the Registrar General of India.
items.why: Continuous enumeration by a part-time local enumerator, an independent half-yearly retrospective survey by a supervisor, then matching and field verification of the mismatches.

items.claim: India's maternal mortality ratio of 93 is reported per 1,000 live births.
items.why: Per 1,00,000 live births, for the period 2019-21, down from 130 in 2014-16. The multiplier and the three-year period are both part of the correct statement.

items.claim: A total fertility rate below 2.1 means India's population is already falling.
items.why: It means fertility is below replacement, not that the population is declining. A young age structure keeps the population growing for decades afterwards — population momentum. India's TFR was 1.9 in 2023 and its population is still rising.

scenes.title: Transfer — a case the lesson has not shown you
scenes.objective: Reason about which system a figure must have come from, and what that implies about its reliability.
scenes.problem: A question asks: 'A newspaper reports that a particular district recorded 12,400 births last year and puts the district's birth rate at 21 per 1,000. Which systems must have supplied the two figures, and what is the weakest link in that birth rate?' Nothing in your notes answers this directly.
hints: Separate the numerator from the denominator and ask which system produces each.
Ask whether the SRS can give you a figure for a single district.
Ask where a district population figure for last year comes from, given when the last census was.

solution.say: The count of 12,400 births is a count of individually registered events for a named district, so it comes from the Civil Registration System. The SRS is a sample and does not publish district estimates; the census does not count births at all.

A rate needs a population denominator. The census is the only complete source for a district population, and the last completed census is 2011, so last year's district population must be a projection rolled forward from 2011.

So the weakest link is the denominator, not the numerator. Registration completeness is now high and measurable; a district population projected sixteen years beyond its census, in a district that may have gained or lost migrants, is not. Any district-level rate computed this way inherits that error.
solution.math: rate = CRS count / projected population → error dominated by the projection

solution.say: A secondary point worth stating: CRS completeness varies sharply by state, so in some states the numerator is also suspect. But as a general answer, the denominator is where the uncertainty sits.
solution.math: Answer: numerator CRS, denominator projected census; denominator is the weak link

scenes.answer: The count comes from the CRS and the population from a projection of Census 2011; the projection is the weaker of the two, which is the concrete cost of a sixteen-year gap between censuses.
scenes.check: The method generalises across this whole topic: for any rate, name the system behind the numerator and the system behind the denominator separately. Most questions about reliability are really questions about one or the other.

scenes.title: What you should now be able to do unaided
scenes.objective: Compress the topic to its facts, its formulae and the one habit that answers the rest.
body: The three systems. Census: a decennial complete count giving the population denominator, under the Census Act, 1948 and the Census Rules, 1990, conducted by the Registrar General of India, ex-officio Census Commissioner, in the Ministry of Home Affairs; a Union subject, entry 69. CRS: continuous compulsory registration of individual events under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, reported within 21 days, amended in 2023. SRS: a continuous sample survey giving India's vital rates, by the dual record system, with no statute behind it.

Census dates. First census 1872, not synchronous; first synchronous census 1881; decennial since; permanent organisation decided May 1949. The 2021 round was postponed owing to the pandemic. Census 2027 is the 16th and the 8th since Independence: Phase I houselisting April to September 2026, Phase II population enumeration February 2027, reference moments 00:00 on 1 March 2027 and 00:00 on 1 October 2026 for Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. India's first digital census, with optional self-enumeration in sixteen languages, caste enumerated following the decision of 30 April 2025, about 31 lakh enumerators and supervisors.

The 2023 amendment. In force 1 October 2023: a national database under the Registrar General, state databases under Chief Registrars, the birth certificate as a single document of proof, registration through the central CRS portal, and use of the database to update the National Population Register, electoral rolls and ration records. CRS 2024 registration completeness: 99.1% of births, 99.4% of deaths in 2024 — measured against SRS-based estimates.

The SRS. Pilot 1964-65, full scale 1969-70. Continuous recording by a part-time local enumerator, an independent half-yearly retrospective survey by a supervisor, matching by the Directorate of Census Operations, field verification of mismatches. 8,839 sampling units and over 8.8 million people by 2023, sized so that IMR has a relative standard error below 15%. Publishes the annual bulletin, the Statistical Report, special bulletins on maternal mortality and causes of death, and abridged life tables.

The figures, with their periods. SRS 2023: CBR 18.4, CDR 6.4, natural growth rate 12.0, IMR 25, TFR 1.9. Sex ratio at birth 917 for 2021-23, females per 1,000 males. MMR 93 per 1,00,000 live births for 2019-21, from 130 for 2014-16, against an SDG target of 70 by 2030.

The formulae. CBR and CDR per 1,000 mid-year population; IMR per 1,000 live births; MMR per 1,00,000 live births. TFR = 5 × Σ ASFR with five-year groups and rates per woman. GRR = TFR × proportion of births female. NRR = GRR × survival of a daughter to the mean age of childbearing, and NRR = 1 is exact replacement. Life table: dₓ = lₓ − lₓ₊₁, qₓ = dₓ / lₓ, e₀ is life expectancy at birth.

The habit. For any rate in this topic, name the system behind the numerator and the system behind the denominator separately. Nearly every question about where a figure came from, or how much to trust it, falls out of that one step.

scenes.objective: Ten unseen questions, drawn 3 easy / 5 moderate / 2 hard.
